newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: OSCE chairman criticises Belarus at summit.
newsitem.headline: OSCE chairman criticises Belarus at summit.

text.p: The chairman of Europe's biggest security organisation criticised Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko at a security summit on Monday, telling him the crisis in his country should be resolved through dialogue.

Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, currently chairman in office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), told the opening session of the summit that he was "deeply concerned" by developments in Belarus.

Lukashenko, who has attempted to strengthen his powers through a controversial referendum in the former Soviet republic, was sitting just a few yards (metres) away at the meeting of more than 50 nations.
"I would appeal to President Lukashenko to resolve the crisis in dialogue with all the parties," Cotti said.

The OSCE and Western countries have called last month's referendum illegitimate and written it off as an unconstitutional grab for power. Lukashenko was greeted coolly when he arrived for the two-day Lisbon summit and other leaders are also expected to criticise him during the summit.
